new: Talk: the people in a shared room who are elsewhere talk to each other through the relay (rooms on a relay only).
Off by default, each device's own. Talk: on asks for the microphone and turns the sound on; Mic: muted only listens.
Open mic: nothing is sent while you are silent, and no controller button is taken.
The rows: the Shared dialog, the headset menu's Circles tab and the phone sheet. Their line says who is talking and who hears you.
People in the same place never hear each other through Talk. In a headset a voice comes from the talker's head.
test: Two people in two places, in one room on the relay: Talk on for both, then speak. In AR, the remote person first presses I am elsewhere on the Debug tab.
In VR, answer the menu's question (are you in the same room as the others?) first: until then the Mic waits.
The Talk row names what a browser lacks: read it on the Quest. If it says this browser cannot use Talk, tell me what it names.
Allow the microphone when asked. In VR the question may show outside the headset view: the line says so after 8 s.
Mic: muted, then on again; Sound off; leave and join the room again. Try with headphones and on the headset's speakers.
untested: Whether Quest Browser has MediaStreamTrackProcessor, AudioEncoder and AudioDecoder, and its microphone prompt inside VR.
Echo: a headset on its speakers, a screen on loudspeakers next to the headsets, two headsets in one room with a remote person.
How voices sound (unheard): Opus at 24 kbit/s, the voice gate on real microphones, the level against the narration, the voice at the head.
Delays and gaps over the relay on home Wi-Fi, venue Wi-Fi and mobile data, and the frame rate with several people talking.
Safari and Firefox: listening only at best. A busy page here sent only part of its voice: watch for voices breaking up.
